title: CSE110: Programming Language I (Java) — BRAC University Aligned
description: Beginner-friendly Java course with real visual diagrams (Python + HTML/JS). Aligned with BRAC University CSE110 modules. Spoon-fed with everyday analogies.

phases.name: Module 1: Flowchart
phases.summary: Learning to plan solutions visually before writing any code — like drawing a map before a road trip.

lessons.title: What is Programming & What are Flowcharts?
objectives: Understand what programming is (giving step-by-step instructions to an obedient robot)
Why we plan with flowcharts before coding (drawing a map before driving)
The basic flowchart shapes: Oval (Start/End), Rectangle (Action), Diamond (Decision), Arrow (Flow)
Drawing your first flowchart: Making a cup of tea
lessons.analogy: A flowchart is a GPS map for your program — it shows every turn and decision before you start driving.

lessons.title: Flowcharts with Decisions and Loops
objectives: Drawing flowcharts that make decisions (Diamond shape: Yes/No paths)
Drawing flowcharts that repeat steps (loops)
Converting a real-world problem into a flowchart step-by-step
Practice: Flowchart for checking if a number is even or odd
lessons.analogy: The diamond shape is a fork in the road — you check a condition and go left or right.

lessons.title: Introduction to Java & Your First Program
objectives: How Java code runs: javac (proofreader) → java (executor)
Writing and running Hello World
What each piece means: class, main, System.out.println, semicolons
Connecting flowcharts to actual Java code
lessons.analogy: javac is the strict spell-checker, java is the robot that follows the checked recipe.

phases.name: Module 2: Variables & Data Types
phases.summary: Teaching the computer to remember things using labeled boxes that only hold specific types of stuff.

lessons.title: Variables: Labeled Boxes in the Computer's Memory
objectives: What is a variable? (A labeled box that stores one value)
Declaring and initializing variables in Java
Naming rules: Why you can't start a name with a number
Changing the value inside a variable (reassignment)
lessons.analogy: A variable is like a labeled jar on a kitchen shelf — 'sugar' jar holds sugar, 'salt' jar holds salt.

lessons.title: Data Types: The Shape of the Box Matters
objectives: int (whole numbers), double (decimals), char (single letter), boolean (true/false), String (text)
Why you can't put text into a number box (type safety)
Type casting: Converting one type to another carefully
Printing and combining different types with +
lessons.analogy: A coin slot only accepts coins, not paper — the shape of the opening decides what fits.

lessons.title: Printing Output & Writing Comments
objectives: System.out.println vs System.out.print (with newline vs without)
Printing variables alongside text
Single-line comments (//) and multi-line comments (/* */)
Why comments are your future-self's best friend
lessons.analogy: Comments are sticky notes on a recipe that the chef ignores — they are just for you to remember why you did something.

phases.name: Module 3: Operators
phases.summary: Using the computer as a powerful calculator — math, comparisons, and logic.

lessons.title: Arithmetic Operators: The Computer's Calculator
objectives: Addition (+), Subtraction (-), Multiplication (*), Division (/)
Integer division trap: Why 5 / 2 = 2 and how to get 2.5
Modulo (%): Finding remainders (useful for even/odd checks)
Increment (++) and Decrement (--) shortcuts
lessons.analogy: Integer division is like cutting a pizza into whole slices — no half-slices unless you ask for decimals.

lessons.title: Comparison & Logical Operators
objectives: Comparison: == (equal?), != (not equal?), >, <, >=, <=
The critical difference: = (put in box) vs == (check if same)
Logical AND (&&), OR (||), NOT (!)
Combining conditions: 'Is age > 18 AND has license?'
lessons.analogy: = is like putting a letter IN a mailbox. == is like asking 'Is there a letter in the mailbox?'

phases.name: Module 4: User Input & Errors in Java
phases.summary: Making your programs interactive — listening to what the user types, and understanding error messages.

lessons.title: Scanner: Giving the Computer Ears
objectives: Importing Scanner (import java.util.Scanner)
Reading text (nextLine), numbers (nextInt, nextDouble) from keyboard
Building an interactive greeting program
Building a simple calculator that asks the user for 2 numbers
lessons.analogy: Scanner is like giving your robot a microphone — now it can listen to you!

lessons.title: Understanding Errors: Syntax, Runtime & Logic Errors
objectives: Syntax Errors: Typos the compiler catches before running (missing semicolons, wrong brackets)
Runtime Errors: Crashes that happen while running (dividing by zero, wrong input type)
Logic Errors: The program runs but gives the wrong answer (the trickiest kind!)
How to read error messages calmly and fix bugs step by step
lessons.analogy: Syntax error = misspelled word in a recipe. Runtime error = the oven explodes. Logic error = you baked a cake but it tastes like salt because you mixed up sugar and salt.

phases.name: Module 5: Branching (Conditional Statements)
phases.summary: Teaching your program to make decisions — like choosing which road to take at a fork.

lessons.title: if, else if, and else: The Decision Maker
objectives: The if statement: Do something only when a condition is true
The else branch: What to do when the condition is false
Chaining decisions with else if for multiple options
Nested if statements: Decisions inside decisions
lessons.analogy: If it's raining → bring umbrella. Else if it's sunny → wear sunglasses. Else → just go out normally.

lessons.title: switch Statement & Ternary Operator
objectives: The switch statement for choosing between many fixed options
When to use switch vs if-else chains
The ternary operator (? :) as a shortcut for simple if-else
Practice: Grade calculator and day-of-week printer
lessons.analogy: switch is like a vending machine — press button A1, A2, A3 to get different snacks.

phases.name: Module 6: Iterations (Loops)
phases.summary: Making the computer repeat tasks automatically — no more copy-pasting the same code 100 times!

lessons.title: while Loop: Keep Going Until Done
objectives: Structure of a while loop: condition → body → repeat
Counter-controlled loops (counting from 1 to 10)
Sentinel-controlled loops (keep going until user says stop)
The danger of infinite loops and how to avoid them
lessons.analogy: While there are dirty dishes → wash one dish → check again. When the sink is empty, stop.

lessons.title: for Loop: Counting with Precision
objectives: The 3 parts: initialization; condition; update
Counting upwards and counting backwards
Using for loops to calculate sums, factorials, and averages
Choosing between while and for: When to use which?
lessons.analogy: Do 10 pushups: start at 1, do one pushup, add 1, stop when you hit 10.

phases.name: Module 7: Iterations (Nested)
phases.summary: Loops inside loops — like a clock where the minute hand goes around once for every hour tick.

lessons.title: Nested Loops: Loops Inside Loops
objectives: How nested loops work: the inner loop completes fully for each step of the outer loop
Building a multiplication table with nested for loops
Printing patterns with stars (* triangles, rectangles, pyramids)
Tracing through nested loop execution step by step
lessons.analogy: For each hour on a clock, the minute hand goes around 60 times. That's a nested loop!

lessons.title: break and continue: Controlling Loop Flow
objectives: break: Emergency exit — leave the loop immediately
continue: Skip this round — jump to the next iteration
Using break to find the first match in a search
Common patterns with break and continue
lessons.analogy: break = walking out of a boring movie. continue = skipping a boring scene but staying for the rest.

phases.name: Module 8: String
phases.summary: Working with text — words, sentences, and all the tricks you can do with them.

lessons.title: Strings: Working with Text in Java
objectives: What is a String? (A chain of characters, like beads on a necklace)
String length, charAt, substring, indexOf
Comparing strings: .equals() vs == (a critical Java trap!)
String concatenation (joining strings together with +)
lessons.analogy: A String is like a necklace of letter beads — each bead has a position number starting from 0.

lessons.title: String Manipulation & Common Operations
objectives: toUpperCase, toLowerCase, trim, replace
Splitting strings into pieces (split)
Converting numbers to strings and strings to numbers
Practice: Password validator, word counter, text reverser
lessons.analogy: String methods are like text-editing superpowers — find-and-replace, capitalize, split a sentence into words.

phases.name: Module 9: Array
phases.summary: Storing lists of related data together — like an egg carton with numbered slots.

lessons.title: Arrays: Numbered Boxes in a Row
objectives: Why we need arrays (50 separate variables is a nightmare!)
Declaring, creating, and initializing arrays
Accessing elements by index (starting from 0)
Looping through arrays with for and for-each
lessons.analogy: An array is like an egg carton — 12 numbered slots (0-11), each holding exactly one egg.

lessons.title: Array Operations & Sorting
objectives: Finding min, max, sum, and average in an array
Searching for a value (linear search)
Sorting arrays: Bubble Sort (the simple visual way)
Using Arrays.sort() for quick sorting
lessons.analogy: Sorting is like arranging books on a shelf by height — compare two neighbors, swap if needed, repeat.

lessons.title: 2D Arrays: Tables and Grids
objectives: What is a 2D array? (A grid/table with rows and columns)
Declaring and using 2D arrays
Nested loops to traverse rows and columns
Practice: Tic-tac-toe board, student grade table
lessons.analogy: A 2D array is like a spreadsheet — rows and columns, and you say 'row 2, column 3' to find a cell.

phases.name: Module 10: Methods
phases.summary: Creating your own reusable commands — write once, use anywhere.

lessons.title: Methods: Your Own Custom Commands
objectives: Why methods exist (Don't Repeat Yourself!)
Declaring a method: return type, name, parameters
Calling a method from main
void methods vs methods that return a value
lessons.analogy: A method is like a saved recipe card — instead of repeating all the steps, you just say 'follow the pancake recipe'.

lessons.title: Parameters, Return Values & Method Overloading
objectives: Passing information into methods (parameters = ingredients)
Getting information back (return = the finished dish)
Method overloading: Same name, different parameters
Scope: Why variables inside a method can't be seen outside
lessons.analogy: You put bread in a toaster (parameter), press the lever (call), and get toast back (return value).

phases.name: Module 11: Recursive Methods
phases.summary: Methods that call themselves — like a mirror reflecting into another mirror.

lessons.title: Recursion: A Method That Calls Itself
objectives: What is recursion? (Breaking a big problem into smaller identical problems)
Base case: When to STOP (the most critical part!)
Recursive case: The method calling itself with a smaller problem
Tracing recursion step by step: factorial, countdown
lessons.analogy: Russian nesting dolls — open one, there is a smaller one inside. Keep opening until you reach the tiniest doll (base case).

phases.name: Module 12: File I/O
phases.summary: Reading from and writing to files — saving your program's work permanently.

lessons.title: Reading and Writing Files in Java
objectives: Why we need files (RAM is temporary — files are permanent)
Reading text from a file line by line
Writing text to a file
Practice: Reading student grades from a file and calculating averages
lessons.analogy: RAM is the kitchen counter (temporary). Files are the pantry (permanent). When you turn off the stove, counter items vanish, but pantry items stay.
